title: Napoli 1-0 Torino: McTominay the difference in much-needed victory
subtitle: Scott McTominay once again came to Napoli and Massimiliano Allegri's rescue, as his superb finish was enough to see off Torino on Saturday.
paragraphs: Scott McTominay scored the only goal as Napoli ended their three-game winless run in all competitions with a 1-0 victory over Torino at the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona.
Napoli signed off for the international break with defeats to Juventus and then Porto in the Champions League as well as holding league leaders Lazio to a 1-1 draw last time out.
Massimiliano Allegri appeared set to come under further pressure until McTominay popped up with the decisive moment in the second half to lift Napoli up to eighth in the table.
Napoli started brightly and fired off two efforts in quick succession through McTominay, but Torino goalkeeper Lucas Perri was left untroubled after the opening 10 minutes.

Matteo Politano brought a smart stop from Perri moments later before McTominay fired the rebound wide of the goal, with Napoli forced into an early change as Antonio Vergara left the field in tears with a suspected hamstring injury and was replaced by Kevin De Bruyne.
Perri continued to keep Napoli at bay, first tipping another effort from McTominay past the post before springing to his right to thwart Rasmus Hojlund's effort from close range.
Despite being under pressure for most of the half, Torino almost went in at the break with the lead, but Rolando Mandragora's stinging drive from distance rattled the crossbar.
The visitors flew out of the traps after the restart, with Zakaria Aboukhlal firing just wide before Nikola Vlasic almost punished a mistake from Rafa Marin shortly afterwards.

McTominay then stung the palms of Perri once more from the edge of the penalty area while Mandragora's long-range free-kick had to be pushed to safety by Vanja Milinkovic-Savic as both teams upped the pressure in search of the opening goal.

And it eventually came in the 73rd minute as McTominay finally found a way past Perri. The Scotland international collected Noa Lang's pass and was allowed time and space to take aim and pick out the bottom-left corner from 25 yards out and seal the win.
Torino become victim to more McTominay magic

With the pressure on Allegri ahead of kick-off, McTominay looked like the only player capable of making something happen as he huffed and puffed in his quest to try and beat Perri, but he eventually got his reward to continue his fine scoring streak against Torino.

McTominay has now scored four goals in three Serie A games against Torino. His goal also saw Torino become the first opponent McTominay has found the back of the net against in three consecutive appearances in his career.
He also finished with team-high totals for shots (seven), touches in the opposition box (nine) and possession won (eight).

Allegri elected to start De Bruyne on the bench amid speculation of a January exit for the Belgian, but the former Manchester City star proved his worth on the pitch, creating more chances (five) and playing more passes in the final third (24) than any player.

There will, however, still be cause for concern for Allegri and Napoli. The Partenopei mustered an expected goals (xG) total of just 1.66 from their 22 shots, 10 of which were on target, compared to Torino's tally of 0.55 from their 12 attempts.
